name: Bishkek School of Contemporary Art (BiSCA)
known: The Prince Claus Fund calls Borubaeva, and NYU calls Tokmergenova, a co-founder of BiSCA.
The Bulbul residency site lists Zholdosheva as chief curator and a co-founder of the residency.
TRASH festival: Borubaeva co-founded the TRASH Environmental Art Festival in 2009 and co-curates it (Wikipedia).

The fifth edition, "Interpreting the History of Pollution: Art Prospect and TRASH-5", ran from 20 September to 22 October 2023 in Bishkek, produced and curated by CEC ArtsLink, BiSCA and Tazar Kyrgyzstan.
Award to a co-founder: Wikipedia says Borubaeva received a Prince Claus Fund award in 2022.
Co-founder Bermet Borubaeva also co-founded the TRASH environmental art festival in 2009 and co-curates it.

name: Gapar Aitiev Kyrgyz National Museum of Fine Arts
known: Owned and run by the Ministry of Culture, Information, Sports and Youth Policy (SRAS); the culture minister appoints and removes its director (24.kg).
Director Mira Dzhangaracheva left after death threats.

name: Kim? Contemporary Art Centre
known: The centre's about page names Zane Čulkstēna as founder and chair of the board, with Evita Goze as the other board member.

name: Latvian National Museum of Art
known: Building: the main building was built in 1903 to 1905 by the Baltic German architect Wilhelm Neumann, the museum's first director, and was the first purpose-built museum building in the Baltic states.
Director Māra Lāce announced in January 2026 that she would leave on 13 April.
It is a state museum accredited by the Ministry of Culture (muzeji.lv); the Ministry runs the competition for its director (LSM).
In 2021 the director said the museum was state-funded and had lost 630,000 euros of revenue to closure (LSM, via the New European Museum Observatory).

name: Riga International Biennial of Contemporary Art (RIBOCA)
known: RIBOCA1, "Everything Was Forever, Until It Was No More", was curated by Katerina Gregos and used eight sites, among them the former biology faculty and the Andrejsala docks (The Art Newspaper, Wikipedia).
RIBOCA3, curated by René Block, was postponed in 2022 after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
2018: the first edition "is funded by the St Petersburg-based fishing entrepreneur Gennady Mirgorodsky", father of the founder (The Art Newspaper).
Its archived site names 33 sponsors for 2018 and three foundation founders.
Curator Žanete Liekīte campaigned against it; four artists withdrew on 30 June 2023.

name: Arab Image Foundation (AIF)
known: Founded by the photographers Fouad Elkoury and Samer Mohdad and the artist Akram Zaatari.
Programmes: collecting, conservation, digitisation, research, exhibitions and a residency programme.
It has co-led photograph conservation workshops in the region (stated by the foundation;
The current board is Vartan Avakian (chair), Rayya Badran (vice-chair), Donald Choubassi (treasurer), Fabiola Hanna (secretary), Nora Kennedy and yasmine habib (members) (stated by the foundation).

Mellon Foundation: both grants went to the University of Delaware, not to the foundation, which is named as a collaborating partner: $560,000 over 42 months from 9 December 2010 for workshops in photograph conservation in the Middle East, with the Metropolitan Museum of Art as collaborator; and $440
Photographic conservation, critical vernacular archives, Middle East & North Africa visual memory

name: Ashkal Alwan
known: Tohmé is its director.

name: Arete Foundation for Arts and Culture
known: Founded by the poet Khaled Mattawa and his wife, the artist Reem Gibriel (MERIP interview, 17 Nov 2021).

Helped set up the first Tripoli International Poetry Festival in April 2012 (Newsweek). "First Glance", described as Libya's first video art exhibit, ran on 6 and 7 November 2012 at Old City Works in Tripoli's Old City, organised by Arete with Gibriel as executive director (Jadaliyya).

name: Contemporary Art Centre (CAC / ŠMC)
known: Valentinas Klimašauskas took over the centre from its founding director, Kęstutis Kuizinas, in early 2025 (e-flux, 31 July 2025).
Set up and founded by the Lithuanian Ministry of Culture in 1992 (CAC).

name: Casino Luxembourg – Forum d'art contemporain
known: Kevin Muhlen is director general and Ruta Franke deputy director (Paperjam).

Governance: the board of directors is chaired by Delphine Munro, with Claudine Hemmer as vice-chair and members Anne Greiveldinger, Laurence Klopp, Pascal Kremer, Ruud Priem, Louis Reuter, Begga Sigurdardottir and Silvano Vidale.
Site-specific production, digital creation, sound art, speculative ecology, curatorial residencies

name: MUDAM (Musée d'Art Moderne Grand-Duc Jean)
known: Bettina Steinbrügge has been director since 2022 (Lëtzebuerger Journal, 4 September 2026).
After the change, an external audit found structural problems and tensions among staff, and board chair Patrick Majerus resigned in January 2025 (Paperjam).
Paperjam's interview with director Bettina Steinbrügge ("La transformation engendre souvent des frictions") describes Mudam as "Financé à plus de 80% par l'État".
